0_samples: - Chirkov et al. 2026: 621 participants with fitted policies (144 alone, 477 in groups); 103 analysed groups (65 of 5, 38 of 4); conditions NP/VP/FP x slow/fast; 15 min at 10 Hz (1 Hz features).
- Wu et al. 2025: 128 participants, 32 sessions of 4; 8 solo + 8 group rounds of 120 s per participant (random/smooth environments); 20 Hz.
- Hawkins et al. 2023: Exp 1 682 participants in 294 games, Exp 3 451 participants in 223 games (games with usable first/second halves); group level: 281 games with >= 2 players, 169 with >= 3.

4c_bis_mps_v1_null: ## 4c-bis. Chirkov D-1: null r of the first mean-preserving shuffle, which matched the five per-agent policy parameters (I, S, k, x0, r_max) but NOT persistence (the superseded version; the final ctrl4b_mps in 4c also matches persistence). The higher null r here (vs the final version) shows that persistence carries much of the prediction

4l_mobility_vs_performance: ## 4l. Mobility vs individual performance (Pearson r, no CI; Discussion support). NOTE the direction in Chirkov: persistence is the probability of NOT rotating, so the negative r means that participants who rotate (re-orient) more score higher; "mobility" in Chirkov is rotation activity, whereas in Wu and Hawkins it is translational path length (agents always move forward in the Chirkov task)
